claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a near-homogeneous elemental distribution.
Pre-annealing at sufficiently high temperature will drive Cu segregation to grain boundaries in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Enhanced Cu enrichment at grain boundaries will lead to in-situ formation of Cu-rich oxide films during high-temperature sliding.
Segregated Cu will oxidize preferentially during high-temperature sliding.
Preferential oxidation of segregated Cu will form a thin protective oxide layer at grain boundaries.
The Cu-rich oxide layer will mitigate metal-to-metal contact.
Mitigating metal-to-metal contact will reduce localized plastic deformation.
Mitigating metal-to-metal contact will reduce wear.
Under high-temperature sliding, the pre-annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the untreated coating.
Under high-temperature sliding, the pre-annealed coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation than the untreated coating.
The predicted effects require a high-temperature regime in which oxidation kinetics and diffusion are active.
Significantly lower temperatures may not permit effective Cu segregation or oxide-layer formation.
The magnitude of the wear and deformation changes depends on the extent of Cu segregation and oxide-film formation.
